title.scientific: Ocean Wave Dynamics: From Tides to Global Climate
title.algorithmic: Procedural Ocean Wave Simulation using Gerstner Waves and Perlin Noise

scientific.concept: Ocean waves are periodic disturbances that transport energy across the water surface, primarily caused by wind, gravitational tides, and underwater earthquakes. Wave physics is governed by the wave equation and surface tension and gravity forces.
scientific.analogy: Imagine throwing a stone into a calm pond. The circular waves that expand outward represent how energy is transferred through the water without the water itself being significantly displaced. Similarly, ocean waves transport energy across vast distances.
scientific.real_world_example: Ocean tides are extremely long waves caused by the gravitational forces of the Moon and Sun. In the Bay of Fundy, Canada, the difference between high and low tide can reach 16 meters, the largest tidal range in the world.
key_concepts: Period: time between two crests passing a point
Phase velocity: speed at which the wave propagates
Wind waves: generated by friction between air and water
Tides: waves with ~12.5 hour period caused by lunar gravity
Tsunamis: long-period waves caused by vertical water displacement

algorithmic.algorithm: Gerstner Waves (Trochoidal Waves) sum with Perlin Noise for realistic perturbations

complexity.time: O(n × m) where n is the number of mesh vertices and m is the number of wave components
complexity.space: O(n) to store the ocean surface state

algorithmic.why_this_algorithm: Gerstner waves properly model the circular motion of water particles (not just vertical movement), creating sharper crests and flatter troughs like real waves. Combining with Perlin noise adds natural irregularity.

comparison.gerstner_vs_sinusoidal: Simple sinusoidal waves don't capture the orbital motion of water particles
comparison.fft_vs_gerstner: FFT (Fast Fourier Transform) is more efficient for large-scale oceans but less intuitive
comparison.perlin_advantage: Perlin noise provides high-frequency details that simulate water surface roughness

parameters.name: wave_count
parameters.description: Number of wave components to sum

visualization_hints.color_mapping: Deep blues for troughs, light blue/greenish for crests
visualization_hints.animation_speed: Speed should reflect wave period (long waves = slow motion)
visualization_hints.foam_generation: Appears on crests where slope exceeds threshold
